what_happened: Job 20261101-222517-3kgp ("Commit job records from the real landing queue after each landing (A8)") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found the plan careful and its seams real. Two major findings remained. (1) The plan dates the queue Score at close time. An intervention made between close and landing is then never scored. `intervene` writes no re-score when no Score exists, and the gate allows a re-score only in the commit that adds its intervention. So the plan's "left for a re-score" premise is false, and dating the Score at landing time would fix it. (2) Moving only the Score does not meet section 8 ("records order equals landing order, never refers to an unlanded job") or the reading's "each landed job's records". Every other closing record still commits at close, before the host landing, yet criterion 6 would call job 8 built. The plan raised this as a blocker question for the user, who must answer it and adjust the criteria before production. There were three minor findings: run/mod.rs and main.rs are not among the reading's deliverables, the squash-merge publication limit is understated, and the descendant check in criterion 1 is weak. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist. It does not make the plan trace the request's stated invariant (section 8) through every writer of records and through the gate rules that govern re-scores and ordering. The plan therefore solved one record (the Score) and built its timing on a gate rule it had not read closely. The one-way gap between the invariant and the plan's scope surfaced only as a user question and as critic findings in the last round. Planning has three fixed rounds and keeps no partial plan, so a late structural finding loses all the planning spend. A question the code and design doc could settle (which records commit when) was passed to the user instead.
prevention: Add a required step to planning for any change to record commit timing or order. The plan must list every record writer on the close and landing path (Score, verification, candidate, intervention, others). For each writer it must state when the record commits, which gate rule (append-only, re-score only with an intervention, ordering) allows that, and which clause of the governing invariant it satisfies. A mechanical check should reject a plan whose acceptance demonstrations name only part of that set. The critic's first-round findings of this kind should go back to the planner as required repairs. A question that a design doc line or the gate code settles must be answered from there and not raised to the user. Partial plans should also be kept so a late round does not discard the whole spend.
proposed_request: Make the real landing queue commit all of each job's closing records (Score, verification, candidate and any intervention re-score) in landing order, after that job's landing and never before it, so that the records order equals the landing order and no record refers to an unlanded job, as docs/design/async-drain.md section 8 requires. Outcome: after a drain of several jobs, the records branch shows each landed job's records in the same order the jobs landed, and an intervention made between a job's close and its landing is scored. Date the queue Score at landing time. Trace every writer of closing records on the close and landing path against the gate rules (Rule::AppendOnly, the re-score rule in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs, and the intervene behavior in manage.rs), and settle from the code which records move. Acceptance: (1) a drain test through the real landing queue with at least three jobs shows every closing record of each job committed after that job's landing and in landing order; (2) an intervention recorded between close and landing produces a Score that includes it, and the gate accepts it; (3) the gate rejects a record that refers to an unlanded job; (4) on a squash-merge host the test states where each job's records appear and what remains unpublished at the end of a drain; (5) the existing close, landing and gate tests still pass. Deliverables may include run/mod.rs, main.rs, close.rs, landing.rs, manage.rs and the gate's jobs.rs, with their tests.
